messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: PROD-DB-HighLatency for redis-cluster-3 — severity: P2 — paging alex chen (primary) and jamie rao (secondary). Link: https://incidents.redwood/prod-db-1234 :rotating_light:
alex chen: seeing the page, pulling up dashboard now. ETA ~2m to confirm impact.
jamie rao: I'm around but on a short call, can take if you need a hard handoff.
maria gonzalez: heads up — CS reports a spike in real-time feature errors for a customer segment. They routed a ticket. Not yet full outage.
sara li: thanks @maria — can we confirm if the errors map to redis latency? I can check traces.
alex chen: checking metrics -> 99th latency up from 30ms to ~800ms on redis-cluster-3 write path. connection errors spiking.

alex chen: quick mitigation plan: 1) switch traffic away from node-3 to node-1/2 via evicting master (runbook step 4). 2) roll a restart if eviction fails. 3) notify customers if >10% error rate.
jamie rao: agree. If you want to swap primary I'm happy to take over the pager after the mitigation — I've got bandwidth in ~10m.
alex chen: I need a short safety pair for the eviction step — @sara do you want to approve and watch?
sara li: on it. Watchlist set. I'll follow logs and KV cache stats.
devops-bot: Runbook invoked: redis-master-failover v2. Command suggestions: 
```
# drain new masters
redis-cli -h node-3 CLUSTER FAILOVER TAKEOVER
# or recommended safe path
scripts/evict-master --cluster redis-cluster-3 --node node-3 --grace 30
```

alex chen: running evict-master --cluster redis-cluster-3 --node node-3 --grace 30 now.

alex chen: eviction started, rebalancer is moving slots. Observability: write latency dropping to ~120ms. errors down from 7% -> 1.2%.
maria gonzalez: customer ticket updated: "Seeing reduced errors, thanks for the quick action." :thumbsup:
jamie rao: nice work. Once this settles can you please hand primary to me? I've got the next 4-hour block and can monitor while alex heads to a quick sync.
alex chen: yep — I'll flag the formal handoff in 8m after we confirm stability for two rolling minutes.
sara li: metrics look stable for 2 minutes, Redis cluster rebalance at 98% slot transfer. No cache thrashing.

alex chen: handing primary to @jamie now — marking in rota. Summary for you: node-3 eviction -> traffic shifted to node-1/2, no config changes, temp client-side backoff in place, alert thresholds adjusted to ignore transient flaps. Runbook link: https://runbooks.redwood/redis-master-failover.
jamie rao: got it, acked. I'll keep an eye for 30m and escalate if it creeps up.
maria gonzalez: FYI I updated the CS ticket and added the mitigation steps.
sara li: small follow-up: let's schedule a post-incident jot to verify why node-3 hit sustained GC; tagging infra team.

alex chen: thanks all. quick note for the shift: I'm heading to a 30m back-to-back, jamie you are primary, sara secondary for the next 4 hours. If anyone gets pages, page jamie first then sara.
jamie rao: confirmed. I'll update the oncall doc and ping infra for a deeper RCA tomorrow.
oncall-bot: Incident closed (P2) — cause: node-3 CPU/Gc spike -> master eviction -> traffic shift mitigated. Duration: 12m. Docs: https://incidents.redwood/prod-db-1234/summary

sara li: thanks team — nice quick coordination. Follow-up actions: 1) infra to inspect GC config, 2) add a soft throttle to client writer to smooth spikes, 3) add a detection rule for >300ms 99th on redis writes.
alex chen: adding those to the postmortem checklist. I'm logging the quick mitigation commands in the runbook as an example snippet.
jamie rao: copying to rota notes and pinging infra in #eng-infra. I'm primary now, reach me if anything else. :phone:"
